Incorporating July 2024 SLOOS insights shifts the read toward more restraint. Banks reported standards that remained tight or tightened further for C&I and CRE loans with weaker demand; consumer credit (credit cards, autos, other) also saw tighter standards and softer demand, and RRE demand was weaker with standards little changed on net. This indicates restrictive credit supply and softer credit demand, adding headwinds to growth and reinforcing the FOMC’s “higher-for-longer” stance and the financial stability vulnerabilities flagged in the FSR. Net effect: the initially slightly positive macro tone is tempered toward neutral.
